questions.q: In the Sahel, a barchan dune advances downwind mainly because sand is
options: deposited on the windward slope while the leeward face is eroded
cemented by salt into a series of parallel ridges
moved up the gentle windward slope and then slips down the steep leeward face
washed down the dune by sheet flow from the crest
questions.explanation: Wind pushes sand grains up the gentle windward slope of a barchan dune; at the crest the grains avalanche down the steep leeward face, so the dune slowly advances downwind. Sheet flow is not the main process moving desert dunes, and erosion of the leeward face while deposition occurs on the windward side would move the dune in the opposite direction.

questions.q: A river entering a lake slows suddenly and deposits sediment in a fan-shaped body at the point where it enters the lake. This feature is called a
questions.explanation: When a river enters standing water such as a lake, its velocity falls sharply and its load is deposited at the mouth, forming a delta. An alluvial fan forms where a stream leaves a steep upland onto a plain, while a levee is a raised bank beside a river channel and a floodplain is the land covered during floods.

questions.q: The gradual downslope movement of soil in a wet tropical area, shown by bent tree trunks and tilted fence posts, is called
questions.explanation: Soil creep is the very slow downslope movement of soil and weathered material, and it commonly bends tree trunks and tilts fence posts over time. A mudflow or landslide is a much faster mass movement, while a rockfall involves the sudden falling of rock fragments.

questions.q: In a ward in Kano State, 2,700 persons are aged 0–14 years, 3,000 persons are aged 15–64 years, and 300 persons are aged 65 years and above. What is the dependency ratio per 100 working-age persons?
questions.explanation: The dependent population is 2,700 + 300 = 3,000, while the working-age population is 3,000. The dependency ratio is (3,000 ÷ 3,000) × 100 = 100 dependents per 100 working-age persons. A value of 90 would result from counting only those aged 0–14, and 50 would result from dividing dependents by the whole population.

questions.q: A market in Onitsha generates large quantities of vegetable waste. Which method both reduces waste and produces useful manure?
options: Burning the waste in open dumps
Sealing it in plastic bags and burying it
Composting the waste in pits and applying the compost to farms
questions.explanation: Composting decomposes organic market waste into manure that can improve farmland, so it reduces waste while producing a useful material. Burning wastes nutrients and causes air pollution, dumping in drains blocks them, and sealing waste in plastic bags prevents useful decomposition.

questions.q: A farmer in Kaduna applies 300 kg of NPK 20:10:10 fertilizer per hectare to a 2 ha maize field. How much phosphorus (P₂O₅) is applied in total?
questions.explanation: The fertilizer contains 10% P₂O₅, so one hectare receives 300 kg × 10% = 30 kg of P₂O₅. For 2 hectares the total is 30 kg × 2 = 60 kg. The value 120 kg would come from mistakenly using the 20% nitrogen figure for phosphorus.

questions.q: Which feature best describes plantation agriculture as practised in parts of southern Nigeria?
options: Smallholdings where most crops are consumed by the farmer's family
Farming that moves every year after soil exhaustion
Large estates with capital investment, hired labour and crops mainly for export
Rearing livestock on natural pasture for local meat supply
questions.explanation: Plantation agriculture is large-scale and commercial, with capital, hired labour and crops such as oil palm, rubber or cocoa grown mainly for export. Smallholdings producing mostly for family consumption describe subsistence farming, while yearly movement after soil exhaustion describes shifting cultivation.

questions.q: Which practice would most effectively reduce soil salinity on an irrigated plot in northern Nigeria?
options: Adding lime to raise the soil pH
Burning crop residues on the plot before planting
Applying enough water to leach salts and providing drainage
questions.explanation: Leaching with sufficient water moves salts below the root zone, and drainage removes the saline water from the plot, reducing salinity. Increasing irrigation without drainage can raise the water table and worsen salinisation, while lime is used mainly to correct acidity and burning residues does not remove salts.

questions.q: A leather-processing factory in Kano obtains hides and skins from nearby abattoirs before turning them into finished leather. Which type of industrial location is this?
questions.explanation: Hides and skins are bulky and perishable, and processing them into leather reduces weight and spoilage risk. Locating near the abattoirs that supply them therefore reduces transport and storage costs, making the industry raw-material oriented.

questions.q: Which policy is most likely to increase the value obtained from Nigeria's solid minerals before they are exported?
options: Using mineral revenue mainly to import finished goods
Exporting minerals in their raw form to save processing costs
Closing all mines in order to conserve the minerals
Encouraging local refining and fabrication of mineral products
questions.explanation: Refining and fabricating minerals turns ores into higher-value products and creates local jobs and linkages. Exporting raw minerals or importing finished goods keeps most of the value outside Nigeria.

questions.q: The local solar time in Maiduguri, on longitude 13°E, is 14:32. What is the local solar time at a town on longitude 8°W?
questions.explanation: The longitudinal difference from 13°E to 8°W is 13° + 8° = 21°, equivalent to 21 × 4 = 84 minutes, or 1 hour 24 minutes. Since Maiduguri is east of the town on 8°W, its time is ahead, so subtract 1 hour 24 minutes from 14:32 to get 13:08.

questions.q: Calabar lies on longitude 8°E and Dakar on longitude 17°W. When it is 18:00 local solar time in Calabar, what is the local solar time in Dakar?
questions.explanation: The longitude difference from 8°E to 17°W is 8° + 17° = 25°, which corresponds to 25 × 4 = 100 minutes, or 1 hour 40 minutes. Calabar is east of Dakar, so Dakar's local solar time is 1 hour 40 minutes behind 18:00, giving 16:20.

questions.q: Which statement about lines of longitude is correct?
options: The Equator is a line of longitude.
The ground distance represented by one degree of longitude is greatest at the Equator and decreases towards the poles.
All meridians are parallel to one another.
The distance between two meridians remains the same at all latitudes.
questions.explanation: Lines of longitude converge at the poles, so the distance between them decreases from the Equator polewards. Therefore, one degree of longitude covers the greatest ground distance at the Equator and decreases towards the poles.

questions.q: On a map with scale 1:25,000, a straight road measures 12.8 cm. What is the ground distance in kilometres?
questions.explanation: Using the scale, 12.8 cm on the map represents 12.8 × 25,000 = 320,000 cm on the ground. Since 100,000 cm = 1 km, this is 3.2 km.

questions.q: A rectangular farmland measures 5.5 cm by 3.6 cm on a map with scale 1:20,000. What is the actual area of the farmland in hectares?
questions.explanation: The ground dimensions are 5.5 × 20,000 = 110,000 cm (1.1 km) and 3.6 × 20,000 = 72,000 cm (0.72 km). Their area is 1.1 × 0.72 = 0.792 km², and 1 km² = 100 hectares, so the area is 79.2 hectares.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: At local noon on the December solstice, a vertical pole at Ibadan (about 7°N) casts a shadow. In which direction does the shadow point?
questions.explanation: At the December solstice the Sun is overhead at about 23.5°S, which is south of Ibadan at about 7°N. At local noon the Sun therefore appears due south, so the shadow of a vertical pole falls due north.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: Which planet has the highest mean density in the solar system?
questions.explanation: Earth has a mean density of about 5.5 g/cm³, the highest among the planets. Mercury is dense but slightly less so, while Venus and Mars have lower mean densities.

questions.q: A farmer in Mbaise, Imo State, cultivates a steep slope that is losing topsoil rapidly after each heavy rain. Which soil conservation practice will most directly reduce sheet erosion on the slope?
options: Grazing many cattle on the slope throughout the year
Ploughing along the contours of the slope
Removing crop residues and leaving the soil bare
Ploughing in straight lines down the slope
questions.explanation: Ploughing along the contours slows run-off and traps soil moving downhill, so it directly reduces sheet erosion. Ploughing downslope and leaving the soil bare encourage water to wash soil away.

questions.q: In a soil catena in the Nsukka area, the footslope usually has deeper, darker topsoil than the crest mainly because
options: the footslope is much older than the crest
eroded soil materials from the upper slope are deposited there
leaching is strongest at the foot of the slope
rainfall is heavier at the footslope than at the crest
questions.explanation: Downslope movement of soil material causes deposition at the footslope, giving deeper and often darker topsoil there than on the eroded crest. Stronger leaching or heavier rainfall at the footslope would not explain the accumulation of soil material.

questions.q: Which means of transport is best for moving natural gas continuously from Escravos to an industrial estate near Lagos?
questions.explanation: Pipelines can move gases continuously in bulk over long distances, making them suitable for supplying natural gas to industry. Lorries, rail wagons, and aircraft are less efficient for continuous large-volume gas supply.

questions.q: The River Niger is less used for transport between Lokoja and Onitsha during the dry season mainly because
options: the river becomes too salty for boats
the water level falls and sandbanks restrict navigation
the current reverses and carries boats upstream
cargoes cannot be insured in the dry season
questions.explanation: Dry-season low flow lowers the water level and exposes sandbanks, making navigation difficult and unreliable. The river does not freeze, its current does not reverse to carry boats upstream, and insurance is not the main physical obstruction.

questions.q: In pre-colonial Nigeria, a settlement sited on a hilltop with steep sides and narrow paths was most likely chosen for
options: a ready supply of water from a nearby river
access to large areas of fertile farmland
ease of constructing wide roads for trade
questions.explanation: A hilltop with steep sides and narrow paths gave inhabitants a defensive advantage against raiders. Wide roads, extensive farmland, and easy water supply are usually associated with lower, more accessible sites.

questions.q: In many Nigerian towns, the zone between the central business district and the outer residential districts, where old houses are mixed with shops and small workshops, is called the
questions.explanation: The transition zone surrounds the central business district and has mixed, changing land uses, including old housing, shops, and small workshops. The rural-urban fringe lies at the outer edge of the city, not immediately beside the central business district.

questions.q: Which Nigerian border town is the main crossing point on the coastal road from Lagos to Cotonou?
questions.explanation: Seme is the main border post on the coastal highway that links Lagos with Cotonou. Idiroko is another border settlement with the Republic of Benin, but it is not the main crossing on that coastal route, while Jibiya and Gamboru lie on other international boundaries.

questions.q: A farmer near Sokoto wants a cereal crop that can mature within the short rainy season and tolerate relatively dry conditions. Which crop is most suitable?
questions.explanation: Millet is drought-tolerant and matures quickly enough for the short rainy season of the Sokoto area. Cocoa and rubber are tree crops that require a humid forest environment, while rice generally needs much more water.

questions.q: The most direct environmental problem associated with crude oil exploration in the Niger Delta is
options: oil pollution of farmland and creeks
laterite hardening caused by bush burning
questions.explanation: Crude oil spills during exploration and transportation pollute farmland, creeks and fishing grounds in the Niger Delta. Desert encroachment and alkalinization are more closely associated with dryland overgrazing or irrigation, not with petroleum exploration in the humid delta.

questions.q: Which cloud type is most closely associated with thunder, lightning and heavy showers over southern Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Cumulonimbus clouds are deep convective clouds that produce thunderstorms and heavy showers. Cirrus clouds are high and thin, stratus clouds form low sheets, and altocumulus clouds are generally middle-level clouds not linked mainly with thunderstorms.

questions.q: A coastal town at sea level records a temperature of 32°C. Assuming a normal lapse rate of 6.5°C per 1,000 m, what is the approximate temperature at a town 2,000 m above sea level?
questions.explanation: A rise of 2,000 m gives a temperature fall of 2 × 6.5°C = 13.0°C. Therefore the temperature at 2,000 m is 32.0°C − 13.0°C = 19.0°C. The value 25.5°C would result from subtracting the lapse rate for only 1,000 m.

questions.q: The alternate freezing and thawing of water in cracks, leading to the splitting of rock, is known as
questions.explanation: Frost action occurs when water enters cracks, freezes, expands and forces the rock apart; repeated freezing and thawing breaks it down. Carbonation and hydrolysis are chemical weathering processes, while abrasion is the wearing away of rock by moving materials.

questions.q: A spring is most likely to occur where
options: a limestone cave roof collapses and exposes an underground stream
a river deposits coarse sand at the mouth of a delta
a glacier melts at the foot of a mountain
permeable rock rests on impermeable rock and the water table meets the surface at their junction
questions.explanation: Groundwater can pass through permeable rock until it reaches an impermeable layer, then flow out at the surface where the junction is exposed. Delta deposition, cave collapse and glacial meltwater may produce other water features, but they do not describe the usual geological condition for a spring.

questions.q: A town has 18,000 people aged 15–64 and 6,000 people aged below 15 or 65 and above. What is the dependency ratio per 100 people of working age?
questions.explanation: The dependency ratio is (6,000 ÷ 18,000) × 100 = 33.3 dependants per 100 working-age people. Using 18,000 as the numerator would give a much larger and incorrect value.

questions.q: Repeated late dry-season bush burning is common in a farming district near Kontagora. Which consequence most directly reduces long-term soil productivity?
options: Rapid weathering of bedrock into new soil
Greater infiltration of rainwater into the subsoil
Loss of soil organic matter and increased exposure of topsoil to erosion
A permanent increase in available phosphorus from ash
questions.explanation: Repeated burning destroys humus and leaves the soil surface bare, making it more vulnerable to erosion and nutrient loss. The ash may give a short-term nutrient boost, but it does not cause a permanent increase in available phosphorus.

questions.q: A neighbourhood in Enugu with many concrete compounds often experiences flash floods after heavy rain. Which change would most effectively reduce local surface runoff?
options: Clearing all roadside grasses and trees
Building higher walls around each compound
Covering open drains with concrete slabs
Replacing part of the concrete surfaces with permeable paving and planted strips
questions.explanation: Permeable paving and planted strips allow rainwater to soak into the ground and slow its movement, reducing surface runoff. Higher walls and covered drains may merely redirect the water, while clearing vegetation usually increases runoff and erosion.

questions.q: A forest reserve in Cross River State is under pressure from villagers collecting fuelwood and clearing small plots for farming. Which measure is most likely to conserve the forest while meeting local needs?
options: Encouraging shifting cultivation within the reserve boundary
Converting the reserve into large-scale plantations
Establishing community woodlots and promoting efficient cooking stoves
Banning all entry into the reserve without providing alternatives
questions.explanation: Community woodlots and efficient stoves reduce pressure on the reserve by supplying fuelwood and lowering wood consumption. A total ban without alternatives is difficult to enforce, while plantations and shifting cultivation inside the reserve would further damage the forest.

questions.q: A smallholder in a humid area of Ogun State plants maize, cassava and melon together in the same field. Which advantage of this practice is most reliable?
options: It eliminates the need for weeding and pest control
It spreads the risk of crop failure and uses soil and light resources more fully
It makes all crops mature at exactly the same time
It guarantees higher yields of every crop than sole cropping
questions.explanation: Mixed cropping can reduce the risk of total loss if one crop fails and allows different crops to use water, nutrients and light at different levels. It does not guarantee higher yields for every crop, remove the need for weeding, or make crops mature together.

questions.q: During the dry season, Malam Audu moves his cattle from a drier northern grazing area towards river valleys and southern pastures. What is the main reason for this movement?
options: To find fresh pasture and water as the dry season advances
To sell cattle at the larger southern markets
To avoid the harmattan winds, which are harmful to cattle in the north
To find cooler temperatures in the coastal areas
questions.explanation: This seasonal movement is mainly a response to the shortage of pasture and water in the drier north during the dry season. Trading and temperature are not the primary reasons for the movement of the herd.

questions.q: A vegetable farmer in Kano has a small plot and limited water for dry-season irrigation. Which irrigation method is most suitable for conserving water while supplying the crop?
questions.explanation: Drip irrigation delivers water slowly near the plant roots, so less water is lost through evaporation and deep percolation. Flood and furrow irrigation generally use larger amounts of water, and overhead sprinklers lose water to evaporation and wind.

questions.q: Which of the following activities is a primary industry?
options: Extracting tin ore on the Jos Plateau
questions.explanation: Primary industries extract raw materials directly from nature, and tin mining fits this category. Refining and vehicle assembly are secondary activities, while selling produce is a tertiary activity.

questions.q: The large liquefied natural gas plant at Bonny was developed mainly to make use of natural gas that was previously flared, for which purpose?
options: To refine crude oil into petrol for domestic vehicles
To process and export natural gas as liquefied natural gas
To produce cement from limestone deposits in the Niger Delta
To generate hydroelectric power from the River Niger
questions.explanation: The Bonny plant cools natural gas into liquid form so that it can be transported by ship and sold in export markets. It is not an oil refinery, hydroelectric power station, or cement plant.

questions.q: When local solar time at longitude 60°E is 12:00 noon, what is the local solar time at longitude 30°W?
questions.explanation: The longitude difference is 60°E + 30°W = 90°, which corresponds to 90 ÷ 15 = 6 hours. Since 60°E is east of 30°W, its time is 6 hours ahead, so 30°W is 6 hours behind noon, giving 06:00.

questions.q: Using the June solstice, when the Sun is overhead at about 23.5°N, what is the approximate noon altitude of the Sun at a town on latitude 15°N?
questions.explanation: The difference between the subsolar latitude and the town’s latitude is 23.5° − 15° = 8.5°. The noon altitude is therefore 90° − 8.5° = 81.5°.

questions.q: A map with scale 1:50,000 is reduced to half its linear size. What is the scale of the reduced map?
questions.explanation: Reducing the linear size by half means that 1 cm on the reduced map represents twice the ground distance represented by 1 cm on the original map. Original 1 cm represents 0.5 km, so on the reduced map 1 cm represents 1 km, giving a scale of 1:100,000; 1:25,000 would result from enlargement rather than reduction.

questions.q: A map has a representative fraction of 1:20,000. Which statement scale is correct?
questions.explanation: Using the representative fraction, 1 cm on the map represents 20,000 cm on the ground. Since 20,000 cm = 200 m = 0.2 km, the statement scale is 1 cm represents 0.2 km; 0.02 km is only 20 m and comes from a decimal-place error.

questions.q: Which map scale would show a small village and its surrounding streets in the greatest detail?
questions.explanation: A map with a larger scale has a smaller denominator and shows a smaller area with more detail. The scale 1:10,000 is larger than the other scales, while 1:250,000 is the smallest scale and would show the least street detail.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: During a new moon phase, why is the Moon generally not visible from Earth?
options: The side of the Moon facing Earth is not illuminated by the Sun.
The Moon moves outside the Earth's orbit.
The Earth's shadow falls on the Moon.
questions.explanation: At new moon, the Moon lies roughly between Earth and the Sun, so its sunlit half faces away from Earth. The Earth's shadow falling on the Moon describes a lunar eclipse, not the usual new moon phase.

questions.q: Which soil type is deposited by rivers on floodplains and is important for dry-season vegetable farming along the Niger–Benue valley?
questions.explanation: Rivers deposit fine, fertile alluvium when they overflow their banks, making alluvial soils suitable for floodplain vegetable farming. Lateritic soils are strongly leached and harden on exposure rather than being mainly river-deposited floodplain soils.

questions.q: Which adaptation enables many savanna trees to survive annual bush fires?
questions.explanation: Thick, corky bark insulates the living tissues of savanna trees from the heat of annual grass fires. Buttress roots are mainly a rainforest adaptation for support in shallow soils, not a fire-survival feature.

questions.q: A Lagos importer buys machinery from China for ₦15,000,000. If import duty is 12%, how much duty is paid?
questions.explanation: Import duty is 12% of ₦15,000,000, so the amount is 0.12 × ₦15,000,000 = ₦1,800,000. ₦180,000 would result from using 1.2% instead of 12%.

questions.q: The main advantage of pipeline transport in Nigeria's petroleum industry is that it...
options: can easily be rerouted to serve remote villages
provides door-to-door delivery to individual retail stations
is the fastest mode for carrying passengers
moves liquids continuously over long distances at relatively low cost.
questions.explanation: Pipelines are suited to continuous bulk movement of crude oil, gas and refined products over long distances at relatively low unit cost. They do not provide flexible door-to-door service and are not used for passenger transport.

questions.q: A town in Nigeria has a law court, a university teaching hospital and a large wholesale market. In the settlement hierarchy of its region, the town is best classified as
questions.explanation: Law courts, a teaching hospital and a wholesale market are specialised services with large catchment areas, so they are found in high-order centres. Low-order centres mainly provide simple goods and services to nearby residents, while a satellite town is defined by its relationship to a larger city rather than by its service rank.
